title: Choose Pimeon's visual world
question: The node graph sets the look for the whole app. Every option keeps standard Apple-style controls; the world supplies only type, colour, density and one signature move. Keep the first, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Overprint Course
options.thesis: Your work is a course overprinted on the team's terrain, so your next step is the one thing you can't miss.
options.viewport: Left sidebar and toolbar, phase columns as faint terrain tints, member lanes in quiet ink, and your route overprinted in magenta with the next step ringed.
options.risk: Fewer people know orienteering maps by heart, so the idea carries on clarity rather than recognition.

raised.raise: Zoom is one continuous axis: a single pinch morphs the whole field from phases to steps to cards, with no hard jumps.
Destructive actions sit apart with deliberate empty space around them, never beside a common control.
Focus on me lifts your lane and lets everything else step back and dim, on one spring.
Every status is a drawn mark first and a colour second, so the graph reads in greyscale.

options.label: Interchange
options.thesis: Each member is a coloured line and each dependency is an interchange, so the plan reads like a metro map.
options.viewport: Left sidebar and toolbar, then thick member lines running left to right, with interchange rings where work crosses between people.
options.risk: It is the first idea most people would have for a node graph, and many member colours can get loud in a big plan.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Steps are stars and importance is brightness, so the critical path shines and the rest stays faint.
options.viewport: Left sidebar and toolbar over a navy field, with bright stars on the critical path and your next step ringed in warm red.
options.case: Students may love it, but dark-first feels less natural in daylight study and needs care to stay legible.
options.risk: A starry field can tip into overwhelming or decorative, the two things you asked to avoid.

options.label: Gate Board
options.lineage: Airport departure boards and boarding passes
options.thesis: Steps rank by when they're due, and a change stays lit until you've noticed it.
options.viewport: Left sidebar and toolbar, your next step as a boarding-pass panel, and the graph below with changed nodes held lit in amber.
options.case: Everyone reads a departure board instantly, but it favours lists over the graph, your hero feature.
options.risk: The ranking idea pulls attention away from the graph's dependencies.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: One slider remaps the whole page live.
options.viewport: Giant step names over a tiny readout.
options.case: A graph of many small nodes has no room for giant type, and students don't identify with a foundry.
options.risk: Type would crowd out the plan.
options.kept: One gesture remaps the whole field continuously.

options.label: Developer Console
options.viewport: Tiled panels around a dark graph.
options.case: It suits developers but shuts out students and event planners, and reads as technical.
options.risk: Feels like a tool for engineers only.
options.kept: Destructive actions isolated by deliberate empty space.

options.label: Streaming Wall
options.thesis: The tile you land on grows while the rest dims.
options.viewport: Rows of phase tiles scrolling sideways.
options.case: Pimeon has no poster art, and rows can't show dependencies between people.
options.kept: The focused item lifts while everything else dims.

options.label: Reference Edition
options.thesis: States are printed marks, drawn by a ruling engine.
options.viewport: Two text columns around a centre rail.
options.case: A text-column form can't carry a spatial graph, and it feels scholarly rather than easy.
options.risk: Too bookish for a first-time user.
options.kept: Status readable as a drawn mark, without colour.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean project-management app in the style of Linear or Asana, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Left sidebar and toolbar, with rounded node cards joined by grey connectors on a neutral canvas.
canonCard.risk: Familiar and trustworthy, but it looks like every other planning tool.
